name: Surface Driven Displacement
definition: A displacement technique requiring a monochrome texture map. The displacement amount is the texture's brightness at each point. Each point of the fluid is shifted along the normal of the point's projection on the isosurface of the fluid's Surface channel. The texture is also sampled at the projection point. This ensures all points above or below the fluid surface are displaced in the same direction, producing results more similar to displaced solid geometry surfaces. It is slower than Gradient driven displacement.
